desc:
You have clothes grouped into categories. counts[i] is the number of items in category i. An outfit takes at most one item from each category, and it must contain at least one item.

Return the number of different outfits, modulo 1,000,000,007.

counts = [1, 1, 1] -> 7
counts = [2, 3]    -> 11
counts = [0, 5]    -> 5
counts = [0, 0]    -> 0
hints: For one category with c items, how many choices are there if you may also take nothing from it?
Choices in different categories are independent, so the numbers of options multiply.
Multiply (counts[i] + 1) over all categories, then subtract 1 to remove the empty outfit.
editorial: For each category there are c + 1 options: one of its c items, or nothing. Choices made in different categories do not interact, so the total number of combinations is the product of c + 1 over all categories. That product includes the outfit that takes nothing from every category, so the answer is the product minus 1.
Reduce modulo 1,000,000,007 while multiplying so the intermediate values stay small. The subtraction is done last, adding MOD if needed to keep the result non-negative.
